title: Ulyana and the Cover
premise: Juniper Pemberton, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of his family in row twelve, receives a meeting invitation from a handler who died three days ago. Following it, he is pulled into a covert operation targeting an attack engineered to look like a mid-air accident — one that echoes every detail of row twelve. As Juniper uncovers a conspiracy inside the very agency that once investigated his family's crash, he must choose between protecting his cover and exposing the truth. In the end, he stops the attack at the cost of his own identity, walking away with nothing but the memory of those he lost — and finally, the truth about why they died.
about_author: Sable Fairweather is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reviewing accident reports before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people who dig too deep into things meant to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Three years after losing his family in the row twelve crash, Juniper works cold cases no agency wants attributed. A calendar invitation arrives from Marcus Hale — his former handler, dead since Friday — scheduling a meeting for tomorrow at 9 a.m. The emotional beat is dread sharpened into compulsion; he decides to go.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Unable to sleep, Juniper rereads the official report on Flight 4471, cataloguing the small inconsistencies he's memorized like scripture. A flashback to the funeral establishes his guilt over surviving a trip he almost took. Emotional beat: grief calcified into method.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. At the meeting site — a shuttered transit depot — Juniper finds not Hale but a woman named Ilse Varga who claims to be Hale's colleague. She tests him with questions only Hale could have answered. Midway through, armed men arrive hunting her. Beat: suspicion curdling into shared danger.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's File
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Escaping together, Ilse reveals Hale left a dead-drop file for Juniper specifically: evidence of 'Operation Cover,' a staged disaster designed to be misattributed to a foreign actor. The target date is eleven days out. Beat: vertigo — his family's crash fits the same signature.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse. Ilse's chapter explains the doctrine of attribution — how accidents are manufactured as messages. She suspects someone inside their own service is running Cover off-book. Beat: professional detachment cracking as she admits she trusted Hale, and Hale is dead.

chapters.title: The Quiet Man
chapters.summary: POV: Antagonist — Director Corben Ash. Ash reviews the operation from a glass office, learning that Hale's file survived and that a grieving investigator has it. He orders a cleanup framed as an internal leak hunt. Beat: cold competence; the reader sees the machinery without seeing its motive.

chapters.title: What Hale Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Decoding Hale's file, Juniper finds a reference to a maintenance subcontractor tied to Flight 4471 — the same firm contracted for the upcoming operation. His family's crash may have been Cover's rehearsal. Beat: rage breaking through investigator's calm.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Realizing he's being followed, Juniper runs a counter-surveillance route through the city, losing a gray sedan but confirming he's marked. He calls no one, trusting no one. Beat: paranoia becoming a skill rather than a wound.

chapters.title: The Subcontractor
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse. Ilse interviews the subcontractor's night manager under pretext, finding falsified inspection logs signed by a man who died two years ago. Someone is signing with ghosts. Beat: triumph turning to unease when she spots a surveillance van outside.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Juniper's credentials are revoked mid-shift; his apartment is searched while he watches from across the street. Officially, he no longer exists. Beat: the price of survival begins — identity stripped, options narrowing to Ilse and a dead man's clues.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the System
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse. Ilse traces the ghost-signature to a personnel file belonging to 'Owen Marsh,' an identity that has been recycled across three agencies for twenty years. Whoever Marsh is, he sits high enough to erase people. Beat: scale revealed — this is institutional, not rogue.

chapters.title: The Safehouse
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Holed up with Ilse, Juniper confesses the truth he's never said aloud: he was supposed to be on Flight 4471, seat 12C, and gave it up for work. Ilse tells him survival isn't guilt. Beat: intimacy forged under threat; the theme surfaces.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Ambushed leaving the safehouse, Juniper is taken by Ash's team and offered a choice: return to his life and forget, or be disappeared. He stalls, planting a tracker on his interrogator's phone. Beat: fear mastered into performance.

chapters.title: The Long Way Out
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse. Believing Juniper compromised, Ilse prepares to run alone — then his tracker pings. She extracts him during a transfer, barely, burning her last safe asset. Beat: trust tested and proven under fire.

chapters.title: Marsh
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Cross-referencing recycled identities, Juniper unmasks Owen Marsh: Deputy Director Alden Reeve, the man who signed off on the original Flight 4471 investigation. The investigator of his family's crash was its architect. Beat: devastation — the ground truth he built his life on collapses.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse. With four days left, Ilse maps the target: a charter flight carrying a peace delegation, scheduled to fail over international waters. Stopping it officially means tipping Reeve's network. Beat: the trap's geometry becomes clear — every road runs through the enemy.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Juniper leaks partial evidence to a journalist as insurance, knowing it will force Reeve to accelerate. It works — the operation moves up forty-eight hours. Beat: gambler's terror; he's now steering the disaster's clock.

chapters.title: Ash Falls
chapters.summary: POV: Antagonist — Ash. Ordered to tie off loose ends, Ash instead confronts Reeve privately and learns the full scope, including that row twelve was personal — a message to Hale. Ash hesitates for the first time. Beat: the machine develops a conscience too late.

chapters.title: Twelve Rows
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Juniper boards the charter as ground crew, racing to plant a mechanical fault report that grounds the flight legally, irreversibly. Reeve's counter-move: a bomb that doesn't need the flight to fly. Beat: climax ignition — the plan and the sabotage collide.

chapters.title: Cover
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper and Ilse alternating. On the tarmac and in the control room, they expose the device, trigger the grounding, and force a public scramble. Ash, choosing sides at last, delivers the internal evidence against Reeve. Beat: chaos resolving into hard-won victory — the attack dies as an unscheduled delay.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Weeks later, from behind anonymity protections, Juniper watches Reeve indicted and Cover dismantled. Flight 4471 is quietly reopened. He learns Hale had been building the case for years and chose Juniper because grief makes the best witness. Beat: vindication shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: Seat 12C
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Juniper visits the crash memorial, leaves the old boarding pass he kept for three years, and walks away unnamed — no badge, no case number, just a man who survived. Final beat: identity surrendered and self reclaimed; the price of survival, paid in full.
